maya (support): Hey team, ACME reported their March invoice is ~12,045,312 tokens but our console 'served_tokens' for acct acme-01 shows ~9,563,210. Customer wants a breakdown and justification. Slacking because they escalated to CSM. invoice: INV-2026-03-ACME

oleg (eng-telemetry): Can you paste the invoice lines and the dashboard time range? Also any request ids or example request traces we can look at? :eyes:

maya (support): Invoice lines sent, dashboard range is Mar 1-31 UTC. One sample request id the customer pasted: req_8f3a2b. They say token counts in the UI + per-route telemetry don't add up to billed total.

oleg (eng-telemetry): Quick hypothesis: we've seen continuous-batcher prefetch accounting cause billed > served when prefix/KV cache avoids generation. I'll run a quick aggregation on metering events for acme-01.

oleg (eng-telemetry): SQL I ran (simplified):
```
SELECT event_type, sum(tokens) as tokens, count(*) as rows
FROM metering.events
WHERE account_id='acme-01' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY event_type;
```
Result: event_type: 'enqueue' tokens=12,048,000 rows=4821
event_type: 'serve' tokens=9,560,000 rows=4802
event_type: 'prefetch' tokens=2,480,000 rows=117

oleg (eng-telemetry): Seems like we have ~2.48M tokens recorded against prefetch/enqueue events that didn't translate into 'serve' tokens because the KV/prefix cache hit path returned without model generation. That explains the delta (~2.48M).

liam (eng-runtime): Short explainer: continuous batching prefetch groups incoming requests to build shared KV cache candidates. Accounting used to increment 'billed' at enqueue time using request.prompt_token_count. If a subsequent cache-hit shortcut returns logits from KV cache, the runtime short-circuits generation but the earlier enqueue accounting was already emitted. So we double-count those tokens unless we mark prefetch events as non-billable. Historically we kept enqueue billing for back-compat (safety net for retry cases), but that interacts poorly with the new prefix-cache short-circuit.

liam (eng-runtime): Example metering event (prod log snippet):
```
{"ts":"2026-03-05T14:22:11Z","account_id":"acme-01","request_id":"req_8f3a2b","event_type":"enqueue","tokens":1024,"batch_id":"b_2045","prefetch":true}
{"ts":"2026-03-05T14:22:12Z","account_id":"acme-01","request_id":"req_8f3a2b","event_type":"serve","tokens":0,"batch_id":"b_2045","cache_hit":true}
```
So billed counted 1024 at enqueue, serve recorded 0 because cache satisfied, net billed appears larger than model work done.

sara (billing): If that's consistent we should issue a one-time credit for the prefetch tokens that were billed but not served. How many tokens are we talking for ACME? The ~2.48M you reported matches their delta. What's the dollar value?

oleg (eng-telemetry): Rough estimate using ACME price tier: $0.0004 per token => 2,480,000 * 0.0004 = $992. I'll produce a precise invoice reconciliation.

liam (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: patch metering pipeline to tag 'prefetch' events as non-billable and stop emitting enqueue-based billed tokens for requests where cache_hit=true. Long-term: move billing emission to serve-time after cache decision. I'll open a PR and a release note.

liam (eng-runtime): PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX - change: metering: don't emit enqueue-bill when prefetch=true AND cache_hit=true; add metric to track ignored_prefetch_tokens.

billing-bot: Automated note: created billing-credit request BC-2026-03-ACME for account acme-01 amount $992.00 (pending finance review).

maya (support): Thanks. I'll update the CSM and customer: offer credit and explain root cause + ETA for fix. ETA for patch?

liam (eng-runtime): Can cut a hotfix to stop enqueue billing for prefetches this week (ETA 48h), full move-to-serve billing in next sprint.

maya (support): Perfect. I'll send a short note to ACME: apology + credit + timeline. Thanks everyone. :heart:
